I have resolved the issue where deferred fields were incorrect when following prefetches back to a parent object.

### Root Cause
When executing `get_prefetch_queryset` on descriptors (`ForwardManyToOneDescriptor`, `ReverseOneToOneDescriptor`, and `ReverseManyToOneDescriptor`), Django manually populates the back-reference cache on the related objects (`rel_obj`) to set the parent instance (`instance`). However, if the nested prefetch queryset on `rel_obj` explicitly specified a prefetch lookup back to the parent object (for example, with a custom `queryset` using `only()` / `defer()`), pre-emptively caching the parent instance on `rel_obj` caused Django to:
1. Skip or overwrite the nested prefetch query for the back-reference.
2. Retain the outer parent instance (which had its own set of deferred fields) on `rel_obj` instead of using the specifically prefetched instance.

### Solution
1. Added helper `_has_prefetch_lookup(queryset, lookup_name)` in [`django/db/models/fields/related_descriptors.py`](file:///testbed/django/db/models/fields/related_descriptors.py#L82) to check if the related queryset contains a prefetch lookup for `lookup_name`.
2. Updated `get_prefetch_queryset` in `ForwardManyToOneDescriptor`, `ReverseOneToOneDescriptor`, and `ReverseManyToOneDescriptor` to check if `rel_is_prefetched` is true before populating the reverse cache. If a nested prefetch for that relation is defined on the queryset, setting the back-reference cache is skipped so that the nested prefetch can fetch and cache the properly filtered/deferred model instance.
